items.title: Thirteen Categories, Forty-Three Kinds: Karma's Full Taxonomic Sweep

items.zh: 如是定異熟業、不定異熟業，異熟已熟業、異熟未熟業。善業、不善業、無記業，律儀所攝業、不律儀所攝業、非律儀非不律儀所攝業，施性業、戒性業、修性業，福業、非福業、不動業，順樂受業、順苦受業、順不苦不樂受業，順現法受業、順生受業、順後受業，
items.en: Thus: karma of determinate ripening and karma of indeterminate ripening; karma already ripened and karma not yet ripened; wholesome, unwholesome, and morally neutral karma; karma bound by moral discipline, karma bound by its absence, and karma bound by neither; karma of the nature of giving, of moral discipline, and of meditative cultivation; meritorious karma, demeritorious karma, and karma leading to the unshakeable formless attainments; karma corresponding to pleasant feeling, to painful feeling, and to neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling; karma ripening in this very life, in the next life, and in some life thereafter.

items.zh: 過去業、未來業、現在業，欲繫業、色繫業、無色繫業，學業、無學業、非學非無學業，見所斷業、修所斷業、無斷業。黑黑異熟業、白白異熟業、黑白黑白異熟業、非黑非白無異熟業能盡諸業。曲業、穢業、濁業、清淨業、寂靜業。
items.en: Past, future, and present karma; karma bound to the desire realm, to the form realm, and to the formless realm; karma of those still training, of those beyond training, and of neither; karma abandoned by the path of seeing, by the path of cultivation, and karma requiring no abandonment at all; dark karma with a dark ripening, bright karma with a bright ripening, mixed karma with a mixed ripening, and the karma that is neither dark nor bright, carrying no ripening at all, capable of exhausting every other kind of karma entirely; crooked karma, tainted karma, and turbid karma; and, finally, pure karma and tranquil karma.

items.zh: 作業者，謂若思業，若思已所起身業、語業。不作業者，謂若不思業，若不思已不起身業、語業。增長業者，謂除十種業。
items.en: 'Karma that is done' means volitional karma, or bodily and verbal karma set going after volition. 'Karma that is not done' means karma without volition, or bodily and verbal karma not set going after volition. 'Karma that is intensified' means all karma apart from the ten kinds.

items.title: Ten Exceptions That Never Intensify, and What Makes Karma Genuinely Deliberate

items.zh: 何等為十？一、夢所作業，二、無知所作業，三、無故思所作業，四、不利不數所作業，五、狂亂所作業，六、失念所作業，七、非樂欲所作業，八、自性無記業，九、悔所損業，十、對治所損業。除此十種，所餘諸業名為增長。
items.en: What are the ten? First, karma performed in a dream; second, karma performed in ignorance; third, karma performed without deliberate intent; fourth, karma performed neither forcefully nor repeatedly; fifth, karma performed while deranged; sixth, karma performed through a lapse of mindfulness; seventh, karma performed unwillingly, at another's command; eighth, karma inherently neutral in nature; ninth, karma diminished through genuine repentance; tenth, karma diminished through an actual antidote applied. Apart from these ten, every remaining kind of karma is called intensified.

items.zh: 不增長業者，謂即所說十種業。
items.en: 'Karma that is not intensified' means the ten kinds of karma just described.

items.title: Deliberate Karma Closes, and the Detailed Taxonomy Begins

items.zh: 故思業者，謂故思已。若作業、若增長業。不故思業者，謂非故思所作業。順定受業者，謂故思已，若作若增長業。順不定受業者，謂故思已，作而不增長業。
items.en: Deliberate karma is karma that, having been carefully considered, is then either carried out or further intensified. Non-deliberate karma is karma performed without such deliberate consideration. Karma certain to be experienced is deliberate karma that has been both carried out and intensified. Karma not certain to be experienced is deliberate karma that has been carried out but not intensified.

items.zh: 異熟已熟業者，謂已與果業。異熟未熟業者，謂未與果業。善業者，謂無貪、無瞋、無癡為因緣業。不善業者，謂貪瞋癡為因緣業。無記業者，謂非無貪、無瞋、無癡為因緣，亦非貪瞋癡為因緣業。
items.en: Karma already ripened is karma that has already yielded its result. Karma not yet ripened is karma that has not yet yielded its result. Wholesome karma has non-craving, non-hatred, and non-delusion as its cause. Unwholesome karma has craving, hatred, and delusion as its cause. Neutral karma has neither of these as its cause.

items.title: Three Kinds of Restraint, and the Twelve Unrestrained Livelihoods

items.zh: 律儀所攝業者，謂或別解脫律儀所攝業，或靜慮等至果斷律儀所攝業，或無漏律儀所攝業。
items.en: Karma bound by restraint is karma bound by the pratimokṣa restraint of individual liberation, or by the restraint that suppresses affliction as the fruit of meditative absorption and attainment, or by uncontaminated restraint.

items.zh: 不律儀所攝業者，謂十二種不律儀類所攝諸業。何等十二不律儀類？一、屠羊，二、販鷄，三、販猪，四、捕鳥，五、罝兔，六、盜賊，七、魁膾，八、守獄，九、讒刺，十、斷獄，十一、縛象，十二、呪龍。
items.en: Karma bound by the absence of restraint is karma belonging to the twelve unrestrained livelihoods. What are the twelve? First, butchering sheep; second, trading in chickens; third, trading in pigs; fourth, trapping birds; fifth, snaring hares; sixth, banditry and theft; seventh, executing condemned prisoners; eighth, guarding a prison; ninth, slandering others for a living; tenth, sentencing prisoners as a magistrate; eleventh, keeping elephants in captivity; twelfth, charming serpents by incantation.

items.zh: 非律儀非不律儀所攝業者，謂除三種律儀業及不律儀類業，所餘一切善、不善、無記業。
items.en: Karma bound by neither is every remaining wholesome, unwholesome, or neutral deed, apart from the three kinds of restrained karma and the twelve unrestrained livelihoods.

items.title: Giving, Precepts, and Meditation, Each Anatomized Fourfold

items.zh: 施性業者，謂若因緣、若等起、若依處、若自性。彼因緣者，謂以無貪、無瞋、無癡為因緣。彼等起者，謂無貪、無瞋、無癡俱行，能捨所施物、能起身語業思。彼依處者，謂以所施物及受者為依處。彼自性者，謂思所起能捨所施物身業、語業。如施性業，如是戒性業、修性業隨其所應應知。
items.en: Karma of the nature of giving has a cause, an arising, a basis, and its own nature. Its cause is non-craving, non-hatred, and non-delusion. Its arising is the intention, occurring together with non-craving, non-hatred, and non-delusion, that is able to relinquish the gift and give rise to the bodily and verbal act. Its basis is the gift itself and its recipient. Its own nature is the bodily and verbal act, arisen from that intention, that actually relinquishes the gift. Karma of the nature of precept-keeping and of meditative cultivation should be understood the same way, each as it applies.

items.zh: 此中戒性業，因緣、等起如前。自性者，謂律儀所攝身語業等。依處者，謂有情、非有情數物。修性因緣者，謂三摩地因緣，即無貪、無瞋、無癡。等起者，謂彼俱行引發定思。自性者，謂三摩地。依處者，謂十方無苦無樂等有情界。
items.en: For precept-keeping karma, the cause and arising are as before. Its own nature is the bodily and verbal act bound by restraint. Its basis is both sentient and non-sentient things. For meditative-cultivation karma, the cause is likewise non-craving, non-hatred, and non-delusion, the actual condition for concentration. Its arising is the intention that, occurring together with these three, gives rise to concentration. Its own nature is concentration itself. Its basis is the realm of beings throughout the ten directions who feel neither pain nor pleasure, and, by extension, those who feel pain or pleasure as well.

items.zh: 又具施戒修者所有相貌，應知一切如餘處說。福
items.en: Further, all the characteristics of one who is accomplished in giving, ethics, and cultivation should be understood as explained elsewhere. Merit

items.title: Merit, Demerit, and the Unmoving Karma of Deep Meditation

items.zh: 業者，謂感善趣異熟，及順五趣受善業。非福業者，謂感惡趣異熟，及順五趣受不善業。不動業者，謂感色、無色界異熟，及順色、無色界受善業。
items.en: Meritorious karma brings a ripened result in a fortunate destiny, together with wholesome karma experienced throughout the five destinies. Demeritorious karma brings a ripened result in an unfortunate destiny, together with unwholesome karma experienced throughout the five destinies. Unmoving karma brings a ripened result in the form or formless realm, together with wholesome karma experienced there.

items.title: Karma Correlated to Pleasant, Painful, and Neutral Feeling

items.zh: 順樂受業者，謂福業及順三靜慮受不動業。順苦受業者，謂非福業順不苦不樂受業者，謂能感一切處阿賴耶識異熟業，及第四靜慮以上不動業。
items.en: Karma correlated to pleasant feeling is meritorious karma, together with the unmoving karma of the first three meditative absorptions. Karma correlated to painful feeling is simply demeritorious karma. Karma correlated to neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling is the karma that everywhere brings a ripened result in the storehouse consciousness, together with the unmoving karma of the fourth absorption and beyond.

blocks.text: Today the treatise lays out a long taxonomy of karma, forty-three kinds in thirteen categories according to Master Cháng Bǎi. It reads like a reference list. The commentary picks out the distinctions a practitioner most needs: which karma is certain to ripen, how restraint works, and how karma relates to the three realms and to feeling.

Not all karma is "intensified" (增長). Ten kinds never intensify: karma done in a dream, unknowingly, unintentionally, neither forcefully nor repeatedly (Venerable Miào Jìng: two separate items, "not forceful" and "not repeated"), by mistake, under compulsion, and so on; also karma that has been repented, or counteracted by its opposite. Everything else, done deliberately, intensifies.

"Karma certain to be experienced is deliberate karma that has been both carried out and intensified." Karma carried out but not intensified is uncertain. Master Cháng Bǎi on how fixed the first is: "It will never pass its time limit; not even the great spiritual powers of the Buddhas can prevent it." (Compare Day 7's criterion: done gladly and without regret, karma is fixed; regretted, it is not.)

This is a sobering and a hopeful passage at once. Certain karma cannot be undone, but most karma is not certain until we intensify it by repetition and approval, so repentance and restraint are effective.

Karma may be bound by three kinds of **restraint** (律儀): the **prātimokṣa** restraint of the precepts; the restraint of meditative absorption, which suppresses affliction; and **uncontaminated** restraint, which comes with the noble path. There are also twelve **unrestrained livelihoods**, such as butchering, hunting, and keeping prisons. One is "slandering others for a living"; Master Cháng Bǎi's modern example is those who write to dig up others' faults or spread them through the media.

Each of the three meritorious activities is analysed fourfold. The basis of meditation is "beings throughout the ten directions who feel neither pain nor pleasure, and so on": Venerable Miào Jìng identifies this as the four immeasurables, love, compassion, joy, and equanimity.

**Meritorious** karma brings ripening in a fortunate destiny of the desire realm; **demeritorious** karma, in an unfortunate one; **unmoving** karma (不動業), in the form and formless realms, where meditative states do not shift to another level. Venerable Miào Jìng: such karma is "projecting karma" (引業), the overall force that leads to the next life.

Karma for **pleasant feeling** includes the desire realm's wholesome karma and the first three absorptions, where, in Master Cháng Bǎi's phrase, the whole body is "drenched with pleasure, as if doused with water". Karma for **neutral feeling** is the karma that ripens everywhere in the storehouse consciousness, and the unmoving karma of the fourth absorption and above. Recall Day 7: the ālayavijñāna's own feeling is always neutral.

quiz.q: The text then lists a long series of karma types. How many, in how many categories, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "There are forty-three kinds of karma, which can be summarised by nature into thirteen categories" — from determinate and indeterminate ripening through pure and tranquil karma.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, how does karma certain to be experienced differ from karma not certain?
options: certain: deliberate, carried out, and intensified; not certain: deliberate and carried out but not intensified
quiz.why: "Karma certain to be experienced is deliberate karma that has been both carried out and intensified. Karma not certain to be experienced is deliberate karma that has been carried out but not intensified." Venerable Miào Jìng: uncertain karma can become intensified when afflictions recur, then revert after repentance — it changes.

quiz.q: How fixed is determinate karma, according to Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: it never passes its appointed time — not even the great powers of the buddhas can prevent it
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "It will never pass its time limit; one will certainly do this — not even the great spiritual powers of the World-Honoured Buddhas can obstruct it." Hence one must repent and apply antidotes before karma becomes intensified.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, what three kinds of restraint bind karma?
options: prātimokṣa restraint, restraint from meditative absorption, and uncontaminated restraint
quiz.why: "Karma bound by the pratimokṣa restraint of individual liberation, or by the restraint that suppresses affliction as the fruit of meditative absorption and attainment, or by uncontaminated restraint." Master Cháng Bǎi: the second is "discipline accompanying concentration," suppressing afflictions; the third "discipline accompanying the path," cutting them off with wisdom.

quiz.q: Among the twelve unrestrained livelihoods is "slandering others for a living." What modern example does Master Cháng Bǎi give?
options: those who write to dig up others' faults or spread them through the media
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: slanderers are "those who specialise in writing articles that find others' faults, or use the media to publicize them," citing the *Satyasiddhi*: harassing good people with anger and no reverence. Venerable Miào Jìng: the "executioner" livelihood refers to headsmen.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, what is unmoving karma?
options: karma bringing ripening in the form or formless realm, and wholesome karma experienced there
quiz.why: "Unmoving karma brings a ripened result in the form or formless realm, together with wholesome karma experienced there." Master Cháng Bǎi: it belongs to concentration and ripens fixed in its own level, unlike desire-realm karma from a scattered mind.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, what is karma correlated to neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling?
options: karma that everywhere brings ripening in the storehouse consciousness, and the unmoving karma of the fourth absorption and beyond
quiz.why: "Karma correlated to neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling is the karma that everywhere brings a ripened result in the storehouse consciousness, together with the unmoving karma of the fourth absorption and beyond." Painful-feeling karma is simply demerit. The ālaya's ripening is always neutral in feeling.
